newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan rupee ends higher on high call rates.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan rupee ends higher on high call rates.

text.p: The Sri Lankan rupee strengthened against the dollar on Friday on high money market rates, ending at 55.70 to the U.S. unit after opening at its previous closing level of 55.79, dealers said.
"The dollar lost ground mainly on banks selling the currency to generate rupees," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Overnight call money closed at 19.5 percent after opening at 17.5 percent. It briefly rose to 21 percent as five big banks continued to borrow, dealers said.
There was little interest in the dollar as attention was concentrated on the money market, brokers said.
Dealers expect the call rate to open higher next week due to continuing demand.
The Central Bank fixed its buying as selling rates at 55.4969 and 56.6181 respectively to the dollar, pushing the U.S. currency up by 3.25 local cents.
